thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging SRE on-call — Tenant=Helios experiencing sustained p99 tail latency > 10s on /v1/stream (streaming stalls). Trigger: alert-streaming-p99-breach. On-call: @emma

emma: Got the page — jumping in. What is the customer impact?

olivia: Observed p95 ~450ms, p99 peaked at 12.4s for the last 15m. Streaming stall count jumped from ~2/min to ~15/min. Error traces show long stalls during chunked-send.

emma: Any recent deploys or config changes for Helios?

infra-bot: No deploys to inference stacks in the last 2 hours. Autoscaler scaled up 2 extra pods ~10m ago due to increased qps.

mike: Helios is single-tenant on dedicated pool dp-hel-01. Traffic spike looks customer-driven — concurrency jumped from 60 to 420 QPS over 10m.

emma: Can someone dump the tail logs and model metrics?

raj: Pasting relevant grep of runtime logs (filtered):
```
2026-03-14T18:05:12Z model=llama-70b-q worker=rtx-4 latency=120ms
2026-03-14T18:06:03Z model=llama-70b-q worker=rtx-4 latency=11.2s stall=streaming_write_timeout
2026-03-14T18:06:14Z model=llama-70b-q worker=rtx-4 latency=12.4s stall=kv-cache-thrash
2026-03-14T18:06:40Z model=llama-70b-q worker=rtx-3 latency=9.8s stall=streaming_write_timeout
```

emma: kv-cache-thrash suggests prefix mismatch or massively long prefixes causing cache churn. Any token size trends?

olivia: Helios prompts spiked in length — median prompt tokens ~18k over last 20m, which is > expected. Many requests include long prefix dumps + few-shot examples.

emma: That explains evictions and cache thrash. For streaming, evicted KV can cause recompute and long blocking. Immediate mitigations: 1) apply tenant-level concurrency cap, 2) route Helios to fallback smaller model (less KV footprint), 3) enable streaming fallback to chunked polling if streaming stalls, 4) temporarily increase dedicated pool capacity. I'll start with (1) and (2).

emma: @infra-bot, apply temporary rate limit to tenant Helios:  max_concurrency=80, window=1s.

infra-bot: Command executed: POST /internal/tenants/Helios/rate_limits {"max_concurrency":80} — 200 OK

emma: @raj, can you add model routing override to send Helios traffic to llama-13b-quant variant? Lower memory KV should reduce thrash.

raj: Doing it now. curl -X POST https://control-plane/internal/routing/overrides -d '{"tenant":"Helios","route":"/v1/stream","target_model":"llama-13b-q","ttl":900}'

raj: Override applied. Confirming traffic shift: 30s in, 60% of Helios streams on 13b.

olivia: Monitoring p99 after routing change — initial signs: p99 dropped to ~3.2s within 2m, stall rate dropped 70%.

emma: Good. Now scale the dedicated pool by +2 nodes to absorb burst and avoid queueing for remaining heavy sessions. @infra-bot please scale dp-hel-01 by +2.

infra-bot: Scaling command: k8s scale --replicas=6 deployment/dp-hel-01-worker — started. New pods provisioning.

mike: Note: model shard placement means some requests still hit the 70b shards for pinned sessions. We should drain those sessions or restart workers after routing fully in effect.

emma: Let's evict LongPrefix cache entries for Helios to reduce immediate thrash. raj, do we have a safe eviction key pattern?

raj: Yes — running: redis-cli -h cache-prod SREM tenant:Helios:prefixes <longkeys> is risky. Safer: use tenant-specific TTL sweep: Schedules expiry sweep for prefix namespace. Executing: POST /internal/cache/expire?tenant=Helios&prefix=longprompt&age_gt=60s

raj: Sweep queued — expected effect within 30-45s.

olivia: After TTL sweep and routing, p99 now stable around 1.1s, streaming stalls at baseline. No errors on model pods.

emma: Great. Customer impact: Helios reported intermittent streaming timeouts in their logs, but most sessions completed on fallback model. No data loss. Account team needs notification. @caroline please prepare an initial customer note: what happened, what we did, guidance on prompt sizes and recommended model.

caroline: Will do; drafting now. I'll highlight concurrency limits and suggest prompt slicing / embeddings for large corpora.

emma: I'm going to hand this to @raj for longer-term stabilization and postmortem. Summary: root cause = unusual prompt storm (very long prefixes) causing KV cache thrash on single-tenant dedicated pool -> streaming stalls increased p99. Immediate mitigations done: tenant rate-limiting, model routing override to 13b-q, cache TTL sweep, scaled pool. Current status = degraded->mitigated.

raj: Acknowledged takeover. I'll monitor for 60m and follow up with RCA checklist:
- collect full trace for evicted keys
- confirm no persistent data corruption
- validate fallback routing rollback plan
- add tenant-specific eval and prompt set test to Redwood Optimize

mike: Also suggest adding an automated guard to detect sustained median token length > 8k and auto-shed or shard differently.

emma: Agree. I'll create a postmortem ticket and include action items: rate-limit templates for single-tenant, routing/rollback runbook, cache eviction safe API, and account communication.

raj: Continuing to watch. If p99 creeps >2s again, I'll escalate and consider draining 70b worker pool and shifting persistent sessions.

caroline: Customer note ready; sending to Helios CSM now. Will update thread with any customer replies.

emma: Passing on-call to raj. On-call handoff: state=mitigated, watch_until=1911115889, contact=caroline (AE). All playbooks executed.

raj: Taking it. :thumbsup: Will bump priority if any regressions.

infra-bot: Auto-log: incident=1911112222 status=mitigated actions=[rate_limit, routing_override, cache_sweep, scale_up]

emma: Thanks team. Postmortem owners: raj (RCA), caroline (customer comms), mike (runtime changes), emma (runbook updates).

olivia: Adding a note — recommend adding a synthetic test that simulates 10k+ token prefixes to catch this early in staging.

raj: Noted. I'll include load test + long-prefix scenarios in the postmortem action items.

caroline: CSM confirmed Helios accepts temporary limits and appreciates quick mitigation.

emma: Closing active page. If anything new pops up, ping in this thread or @oncall.

incident-bot: Incident closed for on-call emma. Duration: 26m.
